segments: Chronography of Bar Ebraya.
And Nikephoros, having reigned foolishly for two years,
and the affairs of the empire having fallen into ruin,
then a general named Alexios Komnenos made a conspiracy with the grandees.
They went out to a suitable place outside Constantinople,
and proclaimed him emperor.
And quickly they returned to the city,
and no one stood against them.
And Alexios entered the palace,
and Nikephoros went out,
and he was repaid according to what he had done,
and was sated with shame and contempt.
And in the year 477,
477 of the Arabs,
while Ibn Marwan was ruling from Mosul as far as the banks of the Euphrates,
and relied upon the forces of the Ma'addites (Arab nomads),
he was not submitting as was proper to the Sultan.
Then the Sultan, Malik-Shah,
sent to Amir Artuq to gather the forces of the Turkmens
and to be prepared for war.
Now Ibn Marwan, when he heard this,
sent to Sharaf al-Dawla ibn Quraysh, the great amir of the Ma'addites, to come to his aid.
And they assembled and came to the vicinity of Amid.
And Artuq also came.
And when Sharaf al-Dawla saw the great number of the Turkmens,
he sent to Artuq and said:
"I am a servant of the Sultan,
and likewise is this Ibn Marwan;
and why is this strife? Rather, I desire that you turn back and I will turn back,
and let there be peace."
Now Amir Artuq agreed to this,
but the Turkmens became angry and grumbled,
saying, "Empty-handed do they wish to return from plunder?"
And at midnight they mounted,
and when it grew light, they fell upon the Ma'addites and killed many,
and the rest fled.
And Sharaf al-Dawla, since no other hope remained to him,
fled and entered
Amid, to Ibn Marwan.
And the Turkmens went to the tents of the Ma'addites,
and took captive and bound women, children, and possessions.
And they put ropes around the necks of the amirs of the Ma'addites whom they caught,
and brought them before the wall of Amid,
and sold them from ten dinars down to less than five.
And a thoroughbred Arab horse was sold for five dinars,
and a camel for one dinar,
and a donkey for five zuzas (dirhams),
and a sheep for half a zuza.
And more than ten thousand spears they broke
and burned under cooking pots.
